sentences.text: As per prosecution story, minor prosecutrix was travelling by a train from Panjab to Jahagar with her parents.
She alighted at Jhansi Railway Station to dring wather where the train departed without her, leaving her strange.

At the station, she was approached by a woman named Rekha (absconding accused) who has falsely promised to take her home but instant approach her to the house of appellant Banwari at Fatehpur, Seekri where she stayed 15 days doing household chores.

It is also alleged that the appellant Banwari took the prosecutrix to Sualal at Chakrana where a team ahs been initated to sale her for Rs.60,000/- to the appellant Dharmendra, other co- accused Rambharosi and Devendra.
Prosecutrix was forced into a marriage with appellant Dharmendra at Shivshankar Colony.
She was found in a room and subjected to repeated rape for seven days before her recovery on 28.07.2013.
Accordingly, offence registered at Police Station Pohari, District Shivpuri.

Case of prosecution is furthyer that MLC of the prosecutrix has been conducted by Dr. Monika Mangal (PW-5) on 29.07.2013 and she opined that the age of the prosecutrix is about 12-13 years and shew as subjected to rape.
3 CRA-390-2014 Her vaginal slide has been prepared and also seized her underwear.
Appellant Dharmendra has also been arrested and on the basis of her MLC has also been conducted.
Thereafter, all the seized articles have been sent for FSL for its chemical examination.
After completion of investigation, charge-sheet has been filed before the Special Judge under the Act, 1990.
Prosecution has examined as many as 10 witnesses while the defence has examined only one witness.
The TrialCourt after scrutinizing the entire evidence available on record convicted and sentenced both the appellants as mentioned hereinabove.
Other co-accused Rambharosi, Devendra and Sualal have been acquitted from all the charges.
Being aggrieved by the impugned jjudgment and conviction, both the appellants have preferred this criminal appeal.
Learned counsel for the appellant Dharmendra has preferred Cr.A. No.365/2014 by stating that the impugned judgment passed by the Trial Court is bad in law.
There is material contradiction in the statement of the prosecutrix and other witnesses.
Ossification test is not conclusive.
The prosecutrix was major at the time of incident.
Prosecutrix has failed to prove her age.
MLC of the prosecutrix has not been supported the allegation of rape.
Co-accused Rekha is not his traceable yet.
Prosecutrix was not recovered from the possession of appellant Dharmendra.
The Trial Court has committed error in not considering the defence of the appellant.
Hence, he prays that the impugned judgment be set aside and appellatn be acquitted from all the charges.

Appellant Banwari has preferred Cr.A.
No.390/2014 by stating that the entire story of the prosecution appears to be imaginary and 4 CRA-390-2014 hypothetical.
The parents of the prosecutrix never lodged his missing person report.

Proscutrix travelled with the appellant Dharmendra different places and lived with him for a cosniderable period but she did not make any hue and cry, therefore, the case appears to be consent matter.
She was leaving with Dharmendra after solemnizing her marriage with him.
There is no allegation that the appellant Banwari has committed rape upon the proscutrix.
Prosecutrix failed to identify the appellant Banwari.

There is material contradiction and ommission in the statement of Banwari Lal Dhakad vs State Of M.P. on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112414499/
2 the prosecution witnesses.

sentences.text: Hence, he prays that the impugned judgment be set aside and appellant be acquitted from all the charges.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State submitted that the impugned judgment passed by the Trial Court is based upon the cogent evidence and proper appreciation of evidence.
The Trial Court has rightly convicted and sentenced both the appellants and same does not call for any interference.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the entire record with due care.
The question which arise for consideration before this Court is firstly whether the prosecutrix at the time of incident was minor ?
Prosecutrix (PW-1) is an illiterate girl.

She categorically stated that her age is about 14 years but she does not know her date of birth, but learned counsel for the appellant on the basis of age of other siblings of the prosecutrix contended that the prosecutirx was major at the time of incident.
He refers the relevant portion of the statement of the prosecutirx (PW-1) and her mother (PW-2) and relative (PW-3) but all these witnesses are illiterate 5 CRA-390-2014 persons.
They could not ascertain the date of birth or age of the prosecutrix, therefore, the prosecution has relied upon the ossification test of the prosecutrix.

Dr. Monika Mangal (WP-5), who has conducted the MLC of the prosecutrix, opined that the age of the prosecutrix appears to be 12-13 years on the basis of her appearance and secondary sexual characters.
Dr. M.L. Agrawal (PW-9), who has conducted the ossification test of the prosecutrix, categorically stated that as per the test, age of the prosecutrix has been found between 16-18 years.
Learned counsel for the appellant Banwari submits that radiological examination is not a conclusive proof.

In support thereof, learned counsel h a s relied upon the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mukarrab Vs. State of U.P. reported in (2017) 2 SCC 210 , and Rajak Mohammad Vs.
State of Himachal Pradesh reported in (2018) 9 SCC 248.

sentences.text: No specific challenge to the ossification test (Ex. P-18) has been made in defence and no other evidence in rebuttal has been filed, therefore, on the basis of the aforesaid cogent evidence, it is proved that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident.

So far as the sexual assault is concerned, prosecutrix (PW-1) categorically stated in her statement that a lady named Rekah who falsely pormised to take her hom, approached her to the hosue of appellant Banwari where she stayed for 15 days, doing household chores.

Thereafter, appellant Banwari, Devendra and Sualal along with other persons solemnized her marriage with Dharmendra,
but no cross-examination, she ctegoricallly stated that she was not ready for the marriage and her marriage has been 6 CRA-390-2014 forcefully solemnized.
Dharmendra filled vermilion in the hairline of the prosecutrix and put a mangalsutra on her, but no hindu rites and rituals or saptapadi has been performed.
Prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident, therefore, alleged marriage cannot be treated as a legal marriage.

sentences.text: Prosecutrix (PW-1) categorically stated that she stayed 7 days at the house of appellant Dharmendra and Dharmendra has committed rape upon her four times.

Although the prosecutrix in her cross-examination stated that Dharmendra has done nothing with her private part, but she categorically stated in other statement that the appellant has put off her clothes and also his own clothes and slept upon her and committed rape upon her.
Learned counsel for the appellant contended that in absence of any evidence regarding penetration specially where in the instant case,, no DNA has been conducted.
Sole statement of the prosecutrix is not reliable.

He placed reliance upoon the judgments of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of ...................................but Dr. Monika Mangal (PW-5) categorically opinned that the prosecutrix was subjected to rape.

Although DNA has not been conducted in the insant matter, but the vaginal slides and underwear of the prosecutrix and seemen slide of the appellant Dharmendra have been sent for chemical examination and as per the FSL report (Ex. P-31), seemen and human sperms have been found in the vaginal slide as well as underwear of the prosecutrix, therefore, on the basis of FSL report, it is duly proved that the prosecutrix was subjected to rape by the appellant.

Although the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Guddu @ Santosh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh vide judgment dated 27.4.2006 passed in Criminal Appeal No.1491/2005 has 7 CRA-390-2014 held that - "it is not necessary that there should be complete penetration of the penis with emission of semen and rupture of hymen.

entities.text: Guddu @ Santosh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Partial penetration within the labia majora of the vulva or pudendum with or without emission of semen is sufficient to constitute the offence of rape as defined in the law.
The depth of penetration is immaterial in an offence punishable under Section 376 IPC."
This citation is completely applicable in the instant case and it has been rightly held by the trial court that the prosecutrix was subjected to rape.

Now after holding that the prosecutrix was minor at the time of incident and she was subjected to rape, only question which ramains to be decided is whether the prosecutrix was subjected to rape by the appellant Dharmendra with help of appellant Banwari ?
Minor prosecutrix (PW-1) has been subjected in a detailed cross- examination along with the question and answer.
She categorically deposed that appellatn Dharmendra has committed rauep with her.

Although she specifically mentioned that appellant Banwari has not committed rape with her but she stated that Banwari and other 3-4 persons had forcefully solemnized her marriage with Dharmendra and handover her to Dharmendra, thereafter, she has been raped by Dharmendra.

Although prosecutrix was some confused with identification of the appellant Banwari in her cross- examination but she stated the name of appellant Banwari in her examination-in-chief as well as her cross-examination.
In the instant case, young girl aged about 15-16 years was left alone in 8 CRA-390-2014 the Railway Station, Jhansi.
Any how, on the false pretext, she was brought to the house of appellant Banwari and thereafter she has been handed over to the appellant Dharmendra.
One can well imagined her trauma after beiing subjected to such sexual harassment.

On reading of entire evidence of the Banwari Lal Dhakad vs State Of M.P. on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112414499/
4 prosecutrix, the Trial Cout has rightly come to the finding that the prosecutrix evidence is cogent and clear to the effect that she has been raped by the appellant Dharmendra.

sentences.text: And Banwari has also played an important role at the time of incident.
Minor prosecutrix was doing household chores in his house and he is having authority to administer upon her as defined in Section 376 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the appellant further contended that the prosecutrix has been tutored by her mother and other witnesses.
There is material contradiction and ommision in her statement.
FIR has also been lodged with inordinate delay.

No report regarding missing person has been lodged in the matter, therefore, her sole statemetn cannot be relied upon but from perusal of the statement of the prosecutrix and other witnesses, it appears that contradiction and omission in their statement are trivial in nature.

Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Haryana reported in 2015 (2) MPLC (Note 7) (S.C.) has held that:
"(A) Criminal Trial - Minor discrepancies on trivial matter, not touching care of the case or not going to the root of the matter - Such discrepancies could not result in rejection of evidence as a whole - Court should ignore such discrepancies which do not shed basic version of the prosecution."
9 CRA-390-2014 On the basis of aforesaid, this Court is of the considered opinion that such contradiction and omission are trivial in nature and same are neither material nor sufficient to disbelief the statement of the prosecutrix which is well supported by other evidence available on record.
Prosecutrix and her family members reside in a.............Chhattisgarh which is about 800 km from the District Shivpuri.

entities.text: Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Haryana reported in 2015 (2) MPLC (Note 7) (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Proscutrix and her mother had no motive to falsely implicate the appellant in the instant case.
It is settled position of law that the conviction can be based upon.

It is the settled position of law that conviction can be based on evidence of solitary eyewitness and omissions or lapses in investigation cannot be a ground to discard the prosecution case, which is otherwise creditable and cogent.
Ocular testimony of the eyewitness cannot be discarded lightly.

(See: State of M.P. Vs. Chakkilal and Another and Ramveer Vs. Chakkilal and Another reported in 2018(4) Crimes 238 SC).
